rules.section: ## Configured production read and private-function endpoint
rules.value: The standard read path admits only FC03 and FC04 requests that have already passed the standard read-operation admission boundary.
rules.reason: The production read path admits only admitted FC03 and FC04 reads.

rules.section: ## Configured production read and private-function endpoint
rules.value: Each endpoint instance has a nonzero lifecycle generation, incremented before a replacement or recovery successor admits a request.
rules.reason: Every successor runs in a new lifecycle generation.

rules.section: ## Configured production read and private-function endpoint
rules.value: Accepted baud rates are 9600, 19200, 38400, 57600, 115200, and 230400; data bits are exactly eight; parity is none, even, or odd; and stop bits are one or two.
rules.reason: Value table of the admitted serial formats.

rules.section: ## Configured production read and private-function endpoint
rules.value: The response timeout is greater than zero and no more than 30 seconds.
rules.reason: Bound of the response timeout.

rules.section: ## Configured production read and private-function endpoint
rules.value: Recovery has one bounded attempt and completes within the response timeout plus t3.5, with an absolute maximum of 60 seconds.
rules.reason: Bound of recovery.

rules.section: ## Configured production read and private-function endpoint
rules.value: An exchange has exactly one send attempt; no retry is admitted by this contract.
rules.reason: One send attempt per exchange; no retry.

rules.section: ## Configured production read and private-function endpoint
rules.value: FC03 and FC04 permit a zero-based offset from 0 through 65535 and a quantity from 1 through 125 registers.
rules.reason: Admitted offset and quantity range of FC03 and FC04.

rules.section: ## Configured production read and private-function endpoint
rules.value: Admission must calculate offset + quantity without 16-bit wrap and require it to be no greater than 65536; otherwise it is NO_SEND before transmission.
rules.reason: Address arithmetic never wraps; an overflow is NO_SEND.

rules.section: ## Configured production read and private-function endpoint
rules.value: Offset 65535 with quantity 1 and offset 65411 with quantity 125 are admitted exact-boundary requests; offset 65535 with quantity 2 is NO_SEND.
rules.reason: Exact boundary examples of the address bound.

rules.section: ## Configured production read and private-function endpoint
rules.value: The normal response byte-count is exactly two times the requested quantity; its RTU ADU is exactly 5 + (2 × quantity) bytes and never exceeds 255 bytes.
rules.reason: Exact normal-response size.

rules.section: ## Configured production read and private-function endpoint
rules.value: The correlation identity binds endpoint generation, request identifier, unit identifier, FC03 or FC04 function, request offset, quantity, and the exact request ADU.
rules.reason: Identity tuple of read correlation.

rules.section: ## Configured production read and private-function endpoint
rules.value: A response satisfies a read only when it arrives in the same unfenced generation and has the matching unit, function, valid RTU integrity, and response shape.
rules.reason: A read is satisfied only by a correlated response of the same generation.

rules.section: ## Configured production read and private-function endpoint
rules.value: A structurally valid, correlated Modbus exception is terminal evidence for its request but does not fence the endpoint generation or require recovery.
rules.reason: A correlated exception is terminal evidence without a fence.

rules.section: ## Configured production read and private-function endpoint
rules.value: A malformed, CRC-failed, late, unrelated, or prior-generation exception is a transport fault and enters quarantine.
rules.reason: An uncorrelated exception is a transport fault.

rules.section: ## Configured production read and private-function endpoint
rules.value: Late, duplicate, unrelated, malformed, CRC-failed, or prior-generation frames enter quarantine and never satisfy a later request.
rules.reason: Quarantined frames never satisfy a later request.

rules.section: ## Configured production read and private-function endpoint
rules.value: Every terminal exchange retains immutable request and response ADU bytes, integrity result, endpoint generation, correlation identifier, unit identifier, function, monotonic send and receipt bounds, retry disposition, and terminal outcome. Failed exchanges retain their available request and transport evidence without inventing response bytes.
rules.reason: Raw evidence retained for every terminal exchange; failed exchanges invent no response bytes.

rules.section: ## Configured production read and private-function endpoint
rules.value: Endpoint identity in public evidence is a stable configured endpoint label, never a local serial path.
rules.reason: Public evidence never names a local serial path.

rules.section: ## Configured production read and private-function endpoint
rules.value: Evidence from a closed, replaced, fenced, or quarantined generation is historical only and cannot authorize, correlate, or be rebound to a successor request.
rules.reason: Evidence of a past generation is historical only.

rules.section: ## Configured production read and private-function endpoint
rules.value: The same endpoint has a separate opt-in private-function path through `RTUProductionConfig.PrivateFunction`: an upstream `RTUPrivateFunctionAdmission` and `MaxResponses` from 1 through 8, both or neither. The zero value (no admission and zero maximum responses) disables private exchanges; a partial configuration or an out-of-range bound is invalid.
rules.reason: The private-function path is opt-in with admission and response bound set together; the zero value disables it.

rules.section: ## Configured production read and private-function endpoint
rules.value: `ExchangePrivateFunction` sends nothing unless that path is enabled, upstream admission approves the endpoint/generation/unit/function/payload candidate, the policy allows exactly one attempt, the unit is not broadcast, and the function code is in the user-defined ranges 65–72 or 100–110 (Modbus Application Protocol Specification V1.1b3, section 5).
rules.reason: Every precondition of a private send, including the user-defined function-code ranges.

rules.section: ## Configured production read and private-function endpoint
rules.value: One endpoint has exactly one in-flight exchange, shared by FC03/FC04 reads and private-function exchanges.
rules.reason: Reads and private exchanges share one in-flight exchange.

rules.section: ## Configured production read and private-function endpoint
rules.value: Each private response frame must complete within `ResponseTimeout`, including first-byte receipt and the t3.5 frame end.
rules.reason: Per-frame bound of a private response.

rules.section: ## Configured production read and private-function endpoint
rules.value: RTU framing enforces t1.5 between bytes and t3.5 frame separation; the frame decoder bounds frame size and checks CRC before unit, function, and exception-shape correlation.
rules.reason: CRC is checked before any correlation.

rules.section: ## Configured production read and private-function endpoint
rules.value: Without a classifier, the first good normal frame is terminal.
rules.reason: Default terminal rule of a private exchange.

rules.section: ## Configured production read and private-function endpoint
rules.value: Reaching `MaxResponses` while still `Continue` is a `response_bound` failure; a terminal frame at the bound is accepted.
rules.reason: Behaviour at the response bound.

rules.section: ## Configured production read and private-function endpoint
rules.value: Response collection allows at most `MaxResponses` frame timeouts plus caller classification time; transport does not bound classifier execution time.
rules.reason: Transport does not bound the classifier; the caller owns the whole-operation deadline.

rules.section: ## Configured production read and private-function endpoint
rules.value: A correlated private-function exception ends the exchange with an error without fencing. Every other failure of a started private exchange fences the generation until `Recover` succeeds: write fault or short write, timeout, cancellation, read fault, malformed/CRC-failed/unit- or function-mismatched frame, classifier error or panic, invalid disposition, or response-bound exhaustion.
rules.reason: A correlated private exception does not fence; every other private failure fences the generation until recovery.

rules.section: ## Configured production read and private-function endpoint

rules.reason: Private evidence keeps every received frame, including partial bytes.
